items.content_html:
Description of changes

Building a NixOS disk image results in an error when compiled without Nix tooling, as indicated by the use of the option nix.enable = false;. Disabling Nix tools through this option not only deactivates general Nix tools but also deletes NixOS installer tools. Consequently, an error is encountered in the nixos/lib/make-disk-image.nix file due to the absence of the nixos-install component.

To address this issue, it is worth noting the availability of the system.disableInstallerTools option, which serves the purpose of disabling installer tools specifically. Therefore, adjusting the configuration by using nix.enable = false; should not interfere with the presence of NixOS installation tools, as this can be managed separately through system.disableInstallerTools.

Component:

nixos/installer/tools: remove nix tooling dependency from nixos config

items.content_html:
Description of changes

With 23.11, nixos-containers won't build unless the option nixpkgs.hostPlatform is set.

Here's a minimal reproducible example:

{
  description = "nixos-containers bug demo";

  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/23.11";

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs }: {
    nixosModules.default = { pkgs, modulesPath, ... }: {
      containers.foo.config = {
        environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.hello ];
        system.stateVersion = "22.05";
      };
      system.stateVersion = "22.05";
    };

    nixosConfigurations = {
      broken = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem rec {
        pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
        modules = [
          "${nixpkgs}/nixos/modules/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix"
          self.nixosModules.default
        ];
      };
    };
  };
}

This results in the following error:

❯ nix flake check
error: Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set.
       You can set nixpkgs.hostPlatform in hardware-configuration.nix by re-running
       a recent version of nixos-generate-config.
       The option nixpkgs.system is still fully supported for NixOS 22.05 interoperability,
       but will be deprecated in the future, so we recommend to set nixpkgs.hostPlatform.

This PR fixes the problem by using pkgs.stdenv instead of nixpkgs.system.

items.content_html:
This PR brings into the nixos-containers module the option to specify a flake instead of a config or a path. This replicates the functionality that nixos-container create <name> --flake <flake> preforms, but through a declarative approach.

During my development on my own server, I found the lack of container flake declarative functionality to be time-consuming in my project. Whenever I had to make bigger changes, I often had to run several commands and tinker with .conf files, when most of it was possible with existing config settings. This PR aims to bridge that gap, by allowing a nixos-container utilizing a flake to be specified declaratively.

This is my first time contributing to NixOS, I have tried to follow the Contributing guidelines as closely as possible, however if I have made any mistakes in this process, please let me know so I can correct. Thank you so much.

Example

Using my own project as an example:

{ lib, config, ... }: {
  containers.devhaj-bot = {
    autoStart = true;

    bindMounts = {
      "/data/blahaj-bot" = {
        hostPath = "/data/devhaj-bot";
        isReadOnly = false;
      };
      
      "/etc/blahaj-bot/token" = {
        hostPath = "/run/agenix/blahaj-bot-token";
        isReadOnly = true;
      };
    };

    flake = "github:transgwender/blahaj-bot/db";
  };
}

This then results in /etc/nixos-containers/devhaj-bot.conf being generated:

FLAKE=github:transgwender/blahaj-bot/db
PRIVATE_USERS=no
INTERFACES=""
MACVLANS=""
AUTO_START=1
EXTRA_NSPAWN_FLAGS=" --bind=/data/devhaj-bot:/data/blahaj-bot --bind-ro=/run/agenix/blahaj-bot-token:/etc/blahaj-bot/token"

items.content_html:
While it's already possible to use secret with Glance (#395551), it can be cumbersome to have separate files for each secret value.

This PR utilizes Glance's ability to include environment variables.

I think we should let the user choose which secret management method do they want to use, rather than deprecating the previous. For example for auth tokens that other services may also use, the older _secret could be beneficial. However for many smaller configuration that you want to keep private, putting them in a single environmentFile could be easier to manage.

Tested this with our glance config
